newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan "appalled" by actions of Zaire rebels.
newsitem.headline: Annan "appalled" by actions of Zaire rebels.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan said Wednesday he was "shocked and appalled by the inhumanity" of the followers of Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila for preventing aid from reaching some 100,000 refugees in the east of the country.

"Assistance is being denied to the 80,000 to 100,000 refugees in the Kisangani area. Promises have been made to the humanitarian agencies which have not been met, and these people are in deplorable conditions," he told reporters after briefing the Security Council on the humanitarian crisis in the Great Lakes region of central Africa.
"I am shocked and appalled by the inhumanity of those who control eastern Zaire to these refugees, most of whom are innocent," Annan said.

He was referring to the fact that most of the refugees are Rwandan Hutus who fled their country after the 1994 massacre of hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Tutsis and moderate Hutus by Hutu troops and militia.
"I have thefeore appealed to the international community to work with me in pressing Kabila and those in the region who back him, to push him to allow assistance to the refugees," Annan said.
It was the latest in a stream of such appeals by the secretary-general and U.N. bodies.

He said he did not think the international community "can stand by as thousands of men and women and children are starved to death. You can kill by shooting or by starvation. Killing by starvation is what is going on," Annan said.
"If Mr Kabila is in charge of his forces, he has to bring them under control. If he is not, he should take measures to control them."
